title: Artifact decide from verdicts — transcribing decisions already made

ground.note: The shipped decide (Completed). It is interactive only and refuses without a terminal (§5.8). It runs the framing questions F1–F5, then a headless handback for the whole revised document, with a corrective resume once. Its checks are §5.19 and §5.21; the body diff must be accepted before anything is written (§5.22). Its exit families are 0/1/5/8/12, it commits in one path-scoped commit, and it writes a decision record. Its non-goals leave the headless mode unspecified and leave out a phax.json key for the decide model.
The original idea: interactive and headless sessions, a caller-owned doctrine, and decisions as JSON. A steering instruction like `rouvre Q3` maps to a decide gesture.

The order of preconditions (migration, Draft, sidecar in sync or hand §9 parses, clean write set, known --question, terminal, Claude model, doctrine, committing identity). Then the interactive session, the handBack with one corrective resume, the diff and confirm, the changed-during-session refusal, the plan cache re-seed, the commit with `Decided-By: operator (<name>)` and `Decision-Id` trailers, and the decision record on every end after spawn. Only a kept session whose `session.json` names claude-code and the same checkout is resumed.

A decided verdict is { kind: decided, chosen, abandoned, why, advocate, principles, reversibility, by: { kind: operator, name }, at, revised }; plans add `phase`. `by` has one variant. The question checks: ids unique, recommendation and chosen name listed options, abandoned is exactly the others.

The decision record manifest: `mode` is the single literal `interactive`; the outcome is committed | declined | undecided | failed, with a commit only when committed. It carries provider, model, effort, usage and the doctrine sources.

For a hand-authored artifact the handback returns a `hand-decision-answer` ($schema, kind, decisions by question id, the whole revised Markdown). phax writes the question blocks and the decision log itself.

The doctrine: E0, C1–C5, S1–S10, the interactive / headless / headless-total modes, and propose-and-escalate. phax sets `by` and `at`. A departing verdict revises the body it implies and names it in `revised`.
The same modes for plans; a plan verdict also names the `phase` it bears on.

Headless authoring resolves model and effort through routing (flag, then phax.json authoring.spec|plan, then the catalog default) and may run on any provider. It keeps the provider session in `session.json` with its provider, for decide to resume.
The kept authoring session: version 1, provider, sessionId, retrySessionId, cwd. Local state only.
The decide model is `--model`/`--effort` or the built-in claude-opus-5-5 / high, and must be a claude-code catalog entry.
DEFAULT_AUTHORING_MODEL and DEFAULT_DECIDE_MODEL are claude-opus-5-5 / high; compliance review defaults to claude-sonnet-5-5. phax.json has `authoring.spec` and `authoring.plan` and no decide key.
The approver union for approve and reopen: machine (kebab-case grant), operator (git user.name), unattributed.
Draft. It reuses the `--by operator | --by machine:<grant>` form and records machine approvals with their grant.
Today decide takes `--question`, `--doctrine`, `--model` and `--effort`, with no `--json` and no `--by`. `phax artifact schema <kind>` prints the spec or plan document schema.

problem:
Interactive decide makes a person open a terminal session to say verdicts they already hold. Often that is "the recommendations, except one". In that session the person decides nothing new; the session exists to transcribe.

A caller without a terminal cannot apply verdicts at all. That covers an agent session working for the person, and a loop such as the steme conductor relaying a person's instruction. decide refuses all of them, so their only paths are a hand edit of the Markdown, which diverges the sidecar and blocks approve, or no decision.

The transcription step already exists and is already headless: phax resumes the session, asks for the whole revised document, checks it and renders it. The terminal stands in front of it, and so does a confirm prompt that only a person at a terminal can answer.

Nor is the transcription made easy to verify. Whoever applied the verdicts must read the result before approving, yet nothing tells them what was transcribed per question. Nothing checks that the chosen option is the one the person gave, or that no other question or section moved.

productGoal.statement:
`phax artifact decide` gains a second mode. A verdicts file carries the decisions a person already made: for each question, the option chosen and the person's note. A headless writer session, under the doctrine, transcribes them into the artifact's revised document, together with the body revisions a departing verdict implies.

phax refuses a bad file before any session. It checks the answer against the file deterministically, writes and commits it without a prompt, and leaves the artifact Draft. It then prints what the caller must read before approving: each verdict as transcribed, and the body diff.

The person decides; the writer only writes it down. A mistake is undone by deciding again or reopening, never by a checker session.
productGoal.guidingRule: The person decides and phax checks the transcription: what the file says is applied as given, nothing it does not name moves, and nothing is approved.

terminology.definition: The input of verdicts mode, in the versioned format phax owns (format id indicative: `decide-verdicts`). It holds `$schema`, the artifact path, and a non-empty list of verdicts, each `{ question, chosen, note }`. It is given as `--verdicts <file|->`.
One entry of the verdicts file. `question` is an id of the artifact's open or arbitrated questions; `chosen` is one of that question's option ids, or `other`; `note` is the person's text or null.
The person's own words about a given verdict: their reason, or a precision on how to apply the chosen option. It is a required key whose value is a non-empty string or null.

The reserved id `other`, implicit on every question of a spec or plan. It never appears among a question's options and is never its recommendation, and no option may use the id. Choosing it means the choice is the one the verdict's note describes, so a verdict choosing it always departs and always carries a note. It never becomes a new option.
A given verdict whose `chosen` differs from its question's `recommendation`.
`phax artifact decide <artifact> --verdicts <file|->`: a headless decide that needs no terminal, raises no framing questions and asks for no confirmation. The person decided before the command ran.

The one headless provider session that verdicts mode runs, under the doctrine skill for the artifact kind and any `--doctrine` file. It returns the whole revised document. It decides nothing: for each given verdict it writes the advocate, principles and reversibility, plus the body revisions and `revised` of a departing verdict.
`phax artifact decide` as shipped by `artifact-decide`. Unchanged by this spec.
Whoever ran verdicts mode: the person, an agent session acting for them, or a loop relaying their instruction. The caller reads the result before approving.
The doctrine's `headless` and `headless total` modes, in which an agent chooses. They are not specified here, and verdicts mode is not one of them.

requirements.title: Verdicts mode
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax artifact decide <artifact> --verdicts <file|->` runs THE system SHALL arbitrate exactly the questions the verdicts file names, each with the option the file gives, without requiring a terminal and without any confirmation prompt.

requirements.title: The verdicts file format
requirements.statement: The system SHALL accept a verdicts file only in its versioned format: `$schema` naming the format at its current shape, the `artifact` path, and a non-empty `verdicts` list whose entries hold exactly `question`, `chosen` and `note` (a non-empty string or null), with unknown keys rejected.

requirements.title: A malformed file is refused
requirements.statement: IF the verdicts file cannot be read, is not JSON, carries no `$schema`, carries one naming another format or shape, or fails the format's schema THEN the system SHALL refuse with exit 12 before any session, naming the `$schema` it read or the first violation by path, and write nothing.

requirements.title: The file must fit the artifact
requirements.statement: IF the verdicts file names an artifact other than the one given, names a question the artifact does not have, names the same question twice, or chooses an id that is neither one of its question's options nor `other` THEN the system SHALL refuse with exit 12 before any session, naming the offending verdict with the artifact's question ids or the question's option ids and `other`, and write nothing.

requirements.title: A departure carries the person's note
requirements.statement: IF a departing verdict, which includes every verdict choosing `other`, has a null note THEN the system SHALL refuse with exit 12 before any session, naming the question and its recommendation, and write nothing.

requirements.title: Today's refusals still apply
requirements.statement: IF any precondition interactive decide checks fails (a live sidecar awaiting migration, an artifact that is not Draft, a diverged or invalid sidecar, a hand-authored §9 that departs from the format, uncommitted changes on the write set, no committing git identity, a refused `--doctrine` file) THEN the system SHALL refuse verdicts mode with exit 12 before any session, as interactive decide does, and write nothing.

requirements.title: Never inside a run
requirements.statement: IF verdicts mode runs inside a phase worktree THEN the system SHALL refuse it with the phase guard's refusal and exit 1 before any session.

requirements.title: Flags belong to one mode
requirements.statement: IF `--verdicts` is given together with `--question`, or `--json` or `--by` is given without `--verdicts` THEN the system SHALL refuse with exit 12 before any session, naming the conflicting flags.

requirements.title: Unnamed questions stay as they are
requirements.statement: WHEN verdicts mode lands THE system SHALL leave every question the file does not name exactly as it was: an open one stays open, and an arbitrated one keeps its verdict and history.

requirements.title: Naming an arbitrated question re-arbitrates it
requirements.statement: WHEN a given verdict names an arbitrated question THE system SHALL give it the new verdict and append its previous verdict to the end of its history.

requirements.title: One writer session
requirements.statement: WHEN every precondition passes THE system SHALL run one headless writer session under the doctrine skill for the artifact kind, followed by any `--doctrine` file. It SHALL resume the artifact's kept authoring session when that session was authored in this checkout on the provider the resolved model runs on, start a new session otherwise, and print which it did.

requirements.title: Model, effort and provider
requirements.statement: The system SHALL resolve the writer session's model and effort from `--model` and `--effort` when given, and from the built-in verdicts default otherwise. It SHALL run the session on the provider model routing resolves for that model, and print the model, effort, their source and the provider.

requirements.title: The writer returns the whole revised document
requirements.statement: The writer session SHALL return the artifact's whole revised document. For each given verdict it SHALL write the advocate, principles and reversibility, and, for a departing verdict, the body revisions the verdict implies, named in `revised`; for a verdict choosing `other`, those are the revisions that apply the choice its note describes.

requirements.title: The person's words are the why
requirements.statement: WHEN a given verdict lands THE system SHALL set its `why` to the note verbatim, or to the question's rationale when the note is null. It SHALL also set the verdict's `by` and `at`, overwriting any value the writer returned for these three fields.

requirements.title: The transcription is checked against the file
requirements.statement: IF the writer's answer fails any check interactive decide applies to a revised document or hand decision answer, chooses for a given question an option other than the one given (`other` included), adds, removes or changes an option of any question, moves or changes a question the file does not name, or changes the body outside the question sections and decision log while no given verdict departs THEN the system SHALL refuse it. After one corrective resume of the same session, the system SHALL fail with exit 5 naming the first violation by path, with the working tree and HEAD unchanged.

requirements.title: `other` is a valid choice
requirements.statement: The system SHALL accept `other` as the `chosen` of a decided verdict on any question, in verdicts mode and in interactive mode, with `abandoned` holding every option the question lists, and SHALL render it as `Decision: other` followed by its why.

requirements.title: `other` is reserved
requirements.statement: IF a question of a spec or plan, in a document an authoring or decide session returns, in a sidecar phax reads, or in a hand-authored §9, lists an option with the id `other` or recommends `other` THEN the system SHALL refuse it, naming the question: exit 5 for a session's document, and exit 12 for an artifact.

requirements.title: Written and committed without a prompt
requirements.statement: WHEN the writer's answer passes every check THE system SHALL write the sidecar, re-render the artifact, and re-seed a plan's extraction cache, keeping its lineage. It SHALL then commit exactly the paths it wrote in one commit, without asking for confirmation.

requirements.title: Deciding never approves
requirements.statement: The system SHALL leave the artifact Draft after verdicts mode, whatever the file says, and SHALL never approve it as part of a decide.

requirements.title: A report to read before approving
Machine-readable report
requirements.statement: WHERE `--json` is given THE system SHALL print the report as one JSON object on stdout and nothing else there, sending progress and warnings to stderr.

requirements.title: The commit says where the verdicts came from
requirements.statement: The system SHALL give the verdicts-mode commit trailers naming the verdicts' arbiter, the verdicts-file channel, and the decision id.

requirements.title: Operator verdicts
requirements.statement: WHEN `--by operator` is given, or no `--by` is given and the command runs from a terminal, THE system SHALL attribute each given verdict to the operator, named by the committing git identity.

requirements.title: A machine is refused
requirements.statement: IF `--by machine:<grant>` is given in verdicts mode THEN the system SHALL refuse with exit 12 before any session, stating that a verdict always comes from the operator and naming `--by operator`, and write nothing.

requirements.title: No terminal, no guessed arbiter
requirements.statement: IF verdicts mode runs without `--by` and not from a terminal THEN the system SHALL refuse with exit 12 before any session, naming `--by operator`.

requirements.title: Hand-authored artifacts
requirements.statement: WHEN verdicts mode runs on a hand-authored artifact whose §9 parses THE system SHALL have the writer return a hand decision answer, and SHALL write the decided question blocks, their Decision blocks and the decision-log entries in place, as interactive decide does.

requirements.title: Rate and usage limits
requirements.statement: IF the writer session ends on a provider rate or usage limit THEN the system SHALL fail in the rate-limit exit family (8) with nothing written.

requirements.title: Artifact changed during the session
requirements.statement: IF the artifact or its sidecar changed while the writer session ran THEN the system SHALL refuse with exit 12 to write the verdicts, leaving the change in place and committing nothing.

requirements.title: Commit failure
requirements.statement: IF the verdicts-mode commit fails THEN the system SHALL report an artifact error with exit 12 and leave the written files uncommitted.

requirements.title: Decision record
requirements.statement: WHEN a writer session ends after spawning and records are enabled THE system SHALL write a decision record. Its manifest SHALL be stamped with its format's shape and say mode `verdicts`. The record SHALL carry: the verdicts file as given, the prompt, the doctrine sources, the landed document, the body diff, the counts arbitrated and departed, provider, model, effort and usage, the outcome (committed or failed), and the commit when there is one.

nonGoals: The doctrine's `headless` and `headless total` modes, in which an agent chooses an option or escalates. Verdicts mode transcribes a person's choices, and those modes stay unspecified.

A checker session run by phax to judge the transcription. The caller reads the report and the diff; a mistake is undone with `phax artifact reopen` and decide `--question` (interactive) or another verdicts file.
Approving as part of deciding. There is no `--approve`, and verdicts mode never touches approval records.
Changing interactive decide: its framing questions, its diff confirmation, its Claude Code-only model and its operator attribution stay as shipped.
Recording a relaying machine in a verdict: a verdict always comes from the operator, a loop relaying a person's instruction runs with `--by operator`, and a verdict's `by` keeps its shape.

Turning an `other` verdict into a new option of its question, listing `other` among a question's options, or editing a question's wording or options from a verdicts file: `other` stays implicit, and its note is the only description of the choice.
A shorthand such as "every other question as recommended": each decided question is written out (subject to §9 q-unnamed).
Turning steering text (`rouvre q-keep`, a chat message) into a verdicts file. That is the caller's job.
Deciding several artifacts in one call.
Framing questions F1–F5 in verdicts mode: nobody is present to answer them.
A phax.json key for the verdicts model and effort (subject to §9 q-model).
Lifting or migrating any document or record written before this change beyond what the shape changes in §6 require.

acceptanceCriteria.name: Verdicts land headless and the artifact stays Draft
acceptanceCriteria.given: a headless-authored Draft spec with open questions q-keep (recommends keep-10), q-scope (recommends per-run) and q-names, and a verdicts file naming q-keep → keep-10 with note null and q-scope → per-run with a note
acceptanceCriteria.when: `phax artifact decide <spec> --verdicts verdicts.json --by operator` runs with stdin not a terminal
acceptanceCriteria.then: It exits 0 without prompting. q-keep and q-scope are in `arbitratedQuestions` with the chosen options given. q-keep's `why` is its rationale verbatim and q-scope's is the note verbatim; both are attributed to the operator by the git user.name. q-names is still open, and the spec is still Draft. The new HEAD commit holds exactly the spec and its sidecar, with the arbiter, `verdicts` channel and Decision-Id trailers. The output lists both verdicts as recommended with their why, lists q-names as open, and prints the body diff and the commit.

acceptanceCriteria.name: A departing verdict revises the body
acceptanceCriteria.given: a Draft spec whose q-keep recommends keep-10, with a requirement and an acceptance criterion written for keep-10, and a verdicts file choosing keep-20 with a note
acceptanceCriteria.then: The committed sidecar holds q-keep with `chosen: keep-20`, `why` equal to the note, a non-empty `revised` naming the requirement and the criterion, and both rewritten for keep-20 with traceability intact. The report marks q-keep as departing from keep-10 and the diff shows the rewritten requirement.

acceptanceCriteria.name: Choosing other applies the note, and nothing else is written
acceptanceCriteria.given: a Draft spec whose q-names lists by-date and by-run, recommends by-date, and has a requirement written for by-date; verdicts files choosing, respectively, other for q-names with the note "Name each log by run id and phase, never by date.", and other for q-names with a null note; a writer answer that adds an option run-phase to q-names and chooses it; and an interactive decide in which the operator chooses other for q-names
acceptanceCriteria.when: verdicts mode runs with each file, and the interactive decide runs and its diff is accepted
acceptanceCriteria.then: The first file lands q-names with `chosen: other`, `abandoned` holding by-date and by-run, `why` equal to the note verbatim, a non-empty `revised`, and the requirement rewritten for naming by run id and phase; q-names' options are unchanged and list no `other`, and the rendered §9 reads `Decision: other`. The null-note file exits 12 naming q-names before any session. The run whose writer adds run-phase resumes the session once, then exits 5 naming q-names' options, writing nothing. The interactive decide lands the same verdict shape.

acceptanceCriteria.name: The id other is reserved
acceptanceCriteria.given: an authoring session returning a spec whose question q-a lists an option with the id `other`; one returning a question that recommends `other`; a hand-authored Draft spec whose §9 question Q1 lists a `- other —` bullet; and a live headless spec written before this change, with no `other` anywhere
acceptanceCriteria.when: each authoring session ends, `phax artifact approve` and `phax artifact decide --verdicts` run on the hand-authored spec, and `phax artifact status` runs on the older spec
acceptanceCriteria.then: Each authoring run exits 5 naming the question and writes nothing. Approve and decide on the hand-authored spec exit 12 naming Q1, with no session spawned. The older spec reads in sync with no migration.

acceptanceCriteria.name: A wrong transcription lands nothing
acceptanceCriteria.given: records enabled, and writer sessions that answer, respectively: q-keep with keep-10 when the file gave keep-20; a document that also moves q-names, which the file does not name; a document that edits §5 while every given verdict follows its recommendation; and a verdict citing `S12`
acceptanceCriteria.when: each session ends and its corrective resume returns the same violation
acceptanceCriteria.then: Each run resumes the session once, then exits 5 naming the violating path. The working tree and HEAD are unchanged, and a decision record with mode `verdicts` and outcome `failed` exists.

acceptanceCriteria.name: A malformed verdicts file is refused before any session
acceptanceCriteria.given: verdicts files that, respectively: are not JSON, have no `$schema`, are stamped `spec-document`, carry an extra key `reason`, have an empty `verdicts` list, and omit `note` on one verdict
acceptanceCriteria.then: Each exits 12 naming the `$schema` read or the first violating path. No session is spawned, and nothing is written or committed.

acceptanceCriteria.name: A file that does not fit the artifact is refused
acceptanceCriteria.given: a Draft spec with q-keep (options keep-10, keep-20; recommends keep-10), and verdicts files that, respectively: name another spec's path, name q-nine, name q-keep twice, choose keep-30, and choose keep-20 with a null note
acceptanceCriteria.then: Each exits 12 before any session. The messages name, in turn: both paths; the artifact's question ids; the duplicate; q-keep's option ids and `other`; and q-keep with its recommendation. Nothing is written.

acceptanceCriteria.name: Today's refusals apply and no terminal is needed
acceptanceCriteria.given: an Approved spec, a spec with a diverged sidecar, a Draft spec with an uncommitted change, a repository with no git user.name, and a phase worktree of a running plan
acceptanceCriteria.when: verdicts mode runs with a valid file and `--by operator` on each, from a script with no terminal
acceptanceCriteria.then: The first four exit 12 with interactive decide's refusals (the Approved one naming `phax artifact reopen`). The worktree run exits 1 with the phase guard's refusal. No run spawns a session or writes anything, and none is refused for lacking a terminal.

acceptanceCriteria.name: Flags belong to one mode
acceptanceCriteria.given: a Draft spec with open questions
acceptanceCriteria.when: decide runs with `--verdicts verdicts.json --question q-keep`, then with `--json` and no `--verdicts`, then with `--by operator` and no `--verdicts`
acceptanceCriteria.then: Each exits 12 naming the conflicting flags. No session is spawned.

acceptanceCriteria.name: Naming an arbitrated question re-arbitrates it
acceptanceCriteria.given: a Draft spec whose q-keep is arbitrated with keep-10 by an operator verdict, and a verdicts file choosing keep-20 for q-keep with a note
acceptanceCriteria.then: q-keep's verdict chooses keep-20, and its history ends with the previous keep-10 verdict unchanged. The other questions are byte-identical in the sidecar.

acceptanceCriteria.name: A verdict always comes from the operator
acceptanceCriteria.given: a Draft spec and a valid verdicts file
acceptanceCriteria.when: verdicts mode runs with `--by machine:roadmap-loop` and no terminal; separately, with `--by operator` and no terminal; separately, from a terminal with no `--by`; separately, with no `--by` and no terminal
acceptanceCriteria.then: The first exits 12, stating that a verdict always comes from the operator and naming `--by operator`, with no session spawned and nothing written. The second and third record each verdict with `by: { kind: operator, name: <git user.name> }`, and `by` keeps its current shape. The fourth exits 12 naming `--by operator`, with no session spawned.

acceptanceCriteria.name: The kept session is resumed only on its own provider
acceptanceCriteria.given: a headless-authored Draft spec whose kept authoring session ran on claude-code in this checkout
acceptanceCriteria.when: verdicts mode runs without `--model`, then again (after reopening and re-deciding) with `--model gpt-6-luna --effort medium`
acceptanceCriteria.then: The first resumes the kept authoring session, prints `resumed authoring session` and `claude-sonnet-5-5 / medium (built-in default) on claude-code`, and loads `phax-decide-spec`. The second starts a new session on the provider routing resolves for gpt-6-luna and prints `new session` with that provider.

acceptanceCriteria.name: A plan is decided and stays executable
acceptanceCriteria.given: a headless Draft plan whose preamble holds open questions Q1 and Q2, and a verdicts file naming Q1
acceptanceCriteria.then: The session loads `phax-decide-plan`. Q1 lands with a `phase` that names one of the plan's phases, and Q2 stays open. The plan passes `phax plans lint`, `phax run` finds its projection without an extraction session, and its lineage in sidecar and frontmatter is unchanged.

acceptanceCriteria.name: Hand-authored artifacts are decided in place
acceptanceCriteria.given: a Draft spec with no sidecar whose §9 format holds open Q1 and Q2, and a verdicts file naming Q1
acceptanceCriteria.then: Q1's block moves to the arbitrated section with its Decision block, one decision-log entry is added, Q2 stays open, and the new HEAD commit holds that file alone.

acceptanceCriteria.name: The JSON report
acceptanceCriteria.given: a Draft spec and a valid verdicts file read from stdin
acceptanceCriteria.then: stdout parses as one JSON object holding the artifact, status Draft, each verdict's question, chosen, recommendation, departs, why, revised and by, the questions left open, the body diff, the commit and the decision id. Nothing else is on stdout.

acceptanceCriteria.name: A limit lands nothing
acceptanceCriteria.given: a writer session that ends on a provider usage limit
acceptanceCriteria.then: It exits 8, and nothing is written or committed.

acceptanceCriteria.name: A concurrent edit is left in place
acceptanceCriteria.given: a writer session during which the spec file is modified
acceptanceCriteria.when: the session returns a valid answer
acceptanceCriteria.then: The run exits 12, the modification is left in place, and no commit is made.

acceptanceCriteria.name: A failed commit leaves the files
acceptanceCriteria.given: a valid writer answer and a commit that fails
acceptanceCriteria.when: verdicts mode writes the artifact and its sidecar
acceptanceCriteria.then: It exits 12, and both files are written but uncommitted.

acceptanceCriteria.name: The record explains the transcription
acceptanceCriteria.given: records enabled and a verdicts-mode commit at `<sha>` that arbitrated two questions, one departing
acceptanceCriteria.then: It shows mode `verdicts`, the verdicts file as given, the prompt, the doctrine sources, the landed document, the body diff, `arbitrated: 2`, `departed: 1`, provider, model, effort, usage and outcome `committed`.

arbitratedQuestions.question: Is the person's note required on every verdict?

options.label: `note` is a required key holding a string or null, and null is refused on a departing verdict
options.abandons: a bare file for departures: a person who departs must write one sentence, even when the reason seems obvious to them

options.label: A non-empty note on every verdict
options.abandons: the one-line case the mode exists for: accepting a recommendation needs a sentence that restates its rationale

options.label: `note` is a string or null on every verdict
options.abandons: the person's reason for a departure: the writer must invent the why of a choice the recommendation argued against

arbitratedQuestions.rationale: A recommended choice already carries its reason: the question's rationale. A departure has no written reason except the person's, and E0 forbids the writer inventing one. The key stays required on every verdict, with null as the explicit "nothing to add", so the format has no optional key.

verdict.why: Adopted as recommended. A recommended choice already carries its reason: the question's rationale. A departure has no written reason except the person's, and E0 forbids the writer inventing one. Refusing a null note on a departure is a condition phax checks before any session.
verdict.advocate: The strongest case for note-free: a note is often an agent's paraphrase of what the person said, so forcing one on a departure can produce a confident-looking reason that is not the person's, where an honest null would say that nothing was recorded.

arbitratedQuestions.question: What becomes of questions the verdicts file does not name?

options.label: They stay as they are: open stays open, arbitrated keeps its verdict
options.abandons: a one-gesture close: a person who wants every question decided must list each one, and an omitted one surfaces only in the report and when approve refuses

options.label: The file must name every open question
options.abandons: deciding part of an artifact now and the rest later, which interactive decide allows with `--question`

options.label: A file-level switch decides every unnamed open question as recommended
options.abandons: a verdict written per question: questions nobody named would be recorded as decided by the person (E0)

arbitratedQuestions.rationale: This matches `--question`, which presents one question alone (C1). The safety stays a condition phax verifies (C4): approve refuses while a question is open. The report and `--json` list the questions left open, so the caller sees them before approving.

verdict.why: Adopted as recommended. Leaving unnamed questions as they are matches `--question` (C1); approve still refuses while a question is open (C4), and the report lists the questions left open. Every decided question is written out, so none is recorded as decided without being named (E0).
verdict.advocate: The strongest case for rest-recommended: "the recommendations, except one" is the most common case, and a file-level switch would state it in one line instead of listing every question.

arbitratedQuestions.question: May a verdict choose an option the question does not list, described in the note?

options.label: `chosen` must name a listed option; the note can only refine how a listed option applies
options.abandons: a person's own answer: an option outside the menu has no path through decide, and the question itself must be re-authored

options.label: A verdict may choose `own`; the writer adds it as a new option with its loss, then chooses it
options.abandons: the deterministic check that `chosen` names a listed option, and the rule that decide never edits a question's options; the new option and its loss would be authored by the writer, unchecked

arbitratedQuestions.rationale: The check that `chosen` is a listed option is what makes the transcription verifiable without a checker (C4). Interactive decide refuses unlisted options too (C1). An option outside the menu rewrites the question, which is a spec change, not a verdict. A precision on applying a listed option fits in the note.

verdict.why: Not own-option as the spec formulated it: no option is written by the agent. `other` is a reserved id, implicit on every question and never listed among its options. Its required note describes the choice. On output the check is: the choice is the given option, or `other`. The document format does not change.
verdict.advocate: The strongest case for refuse, and for the written `other` this verdict replaces: a reader sees no `other` under a question, so only someone who knows the rule can tell the question stayed open to another choice, and only the caller's reading of the diff checks that the body says what the note describes.
revised: §5 r-binding: an id neither listed nor other is refused
§6 verdicts file: chosen may be the reserved other
§6 written other option replaced by a verdict choosing other
§10 settled, constraints: no document shape change, no migration

history.why: Adopted as recommended. The check that `chosen` names a listed option is what makes the transcription verifiable without a checker (C4), and interactive decide refuses unlisted options too (C1). An option outside the menu rewrites the question, which is a spec change, not a verdict; a precision on a listed option fits in the note.
history.advocate: The strongest case for own-option: the right answer is sometimes not on the menu, and re-authoring the question only to add it is a heavy detour for a person who already knows what they want.

history.why: Not own-option as the spec formulated it: no option is written by the agent. Every question lists, written in its options, an option `other` whose label and loss phax fixes, and whose required note describes the choice. On output the check is: the choice is the given option, or `other`. Simpler, and verifiable.
history.advocate: The strongest case for refuse: with `other`, the writer applies to the body a choice nobody wrote as an option, with no loss named and no comparison with the others; only the caller's reading of the diff can check that the rewritten requirements, surface and criteria say what the note describes.
revised: §5 r-note: a verdict choosing other always departs
§5 r-writer: other applies the note's choice
§5 r-checks: chosen is the given option, other included; no option added, removed or changed
§6 verdicts file: chosen may be other
§6 question options and rendered §9: the fixed other option, added
§7 Non-goals: other never becomes a new option
§10 settled, constraints: other, document shapes and migration

arbitratedQuestions.question: Who writes a given verdict's `why`?

options.label: phax sets `why`: the note verbatim, or the question's rationale when the note is null
options.abandons: a why that reads as prose in context: a terse note becomes the recorded reason exactly as typed

options.label: The writer writes `why` from the note or the rationale
options.abandons: a why guaranteed to be the person's: a paraphrase can shift the reason, and only the caller's reading would catch it

arbitratedQuestions.rationale: The why is the one field that states the person's decision, so making it the person's words verbatim is a condition phax guarantees (C4), not something the caller must check by reading. phax already sets `by` and `at` the same way. What the writer still writes (advocate, principles, reversibility, body revisions) is what the report and diff put in front of the caller.

verdict.why: Adopted as recommended. The why states the person's decision, so phax copying the note verbatim (or the rationale when the note is null) is a condition it guarantees (C4), as it already sets `by` and `at`, rather than something the caller must check by reading (E0).
verdict.advocate: The strongest case for writer-writes-why: a terse note becomes the permanent recorded reason exactly as typed, where the writer could turn it into a why that reads in context.

arbitratedQuestions.question: How is a verdict given through a file attributed?

options.label: Always the operator, by the committing git identity; no `--by`; the channel shows only in the commit trailer and the record
options.abandons: an honest arbiter without a terminal: a loop committing under someone's git identity is recorded as that person, the guess approve has refused since its Q3

options.label: `--by operator` is required without a terminal and machine is refused, so a verdict is always the operator's
options.abandons: any trace of the relaying machine in the document: a loop must declare itself the operator, and its grant appears nowhere in the verdict

options.label: `--by operator | machine:<grant>`, required without a terminal; machine records `by: { kind: relayed, grant }`, naming no person
options.abandons: unchanged document shapes: spec-document, plan-document and hand-decision-answer gain a verdict variant. Unless that rides the shape still unreleased at the next cut, every live sidecar must pass `phax artifact migrate-documents` again

arbitratedQuestions.rationale: Choosing `relayed` keeps attribution explicit (E0) and consistent with how approve and reopen take `--by` (C1). A loop never records itself as a person, and a person is never named by a guess. `relayed` is not the doctrine's machine-decides mode: it says a machine carried a decision, not that a machine made it. The shape change is the accepted loss: a union widening that the release cut records, costing at most one known migrate gesture.

verdict.why: A verdict always comes from the operator. Without a terminal, `--by operator` is required and `--by machine:…` is refused. The sidecar format does not change.
verdict.advocate: The strongest case for relayed: a loop like the steme conductor must now declare itself the operator, so nothing in the document, the commit or the record says a machine carried the verdict, while with auto-migrate the shape change would have cost almost nothing.
revised: §7 Non-goals: no relaying machine in a verdict

history.why: Adopted as recommended. `relayed` keeps attribution explicit (E0) and takes `--by` as approve and reopen do (C1): a loop never records itself as a person, and no person is named by a guess (S6). It records that a machine carried a decision, not that a machine made it. The document shape change is the accepted loss.
history.advocate: The strongest case for operator-declared: it changes no document format and forces no migrate-documents run, while the relaying machine's grant can still be kept in the commit trailer and the decision record.

arbitratedQuestions.question: Does the writer session go through model routing, or run on Claude Code only like interactive decide?

options.label: Routed like headless authoring: any provider the catalog maps; the kept session is resumed only on its own provider
options.abandons: one provider rule for one command: interactive decide stays Claude Code only while its verdicts mode runs anywhere

options.label: Claude Code only, like interactive decide
options.abandons: callers on Codex or Vibe: a loop on another provider cannot apply verdicts at all

arbitratedQuestions.rationale: The writer is a headless JSON-answer session, the kind authoring already routes (C1 with the session it most resembles). Interactive decide is Claude-only because of its terminal session, which verdicts mode does not have. `session.json` already records the authoring provider, so resuming on the same provider is a check, not a guess.

verdict.why: Adopted as recommended. The writer is a headless JSON-answer session, the kind authoring already routes (C1). Interactive decide is Claude-only because of its terminal session, which verdicts mode does not have, and `session.json` records the authoring provider, so resuming on the same provider is a check.
verdict.advocate: The strongest case for claude-only: one command keeps one provider rule, the same as interactive decide.

arbitratedQuestions.question: What are the writer's default model and effort, and is there a phax.json key?

options.label: `--model`/`--effort`, else a built-in claude-sonnet-5-5 / medium; no phax.json key
options.abandons: a project-wide setting: a project on another provider passes `--model` on every call

options.label: `--model`/`--effort`, else phax.json `authoring.spec|plan`, else claude-opus-5-5 / high
options.abandons: the cheaper default: every transcription is priced as authoring a whole spec

options.label: `--model`/`--effort`, else a new phax.json `decide.verdicts`, else claude-sonnet-5-5 / medium
options.abandons: an unchanged config surface: a new key, which artifact-decide deliberately did not add

arbitratedQuestions.rationale: Transcribing given verdicts and revising the body they imply needs less judgment than authoring or interactive facilitation. Following the catalog on cost, it takes the tier compliance review already defaults to: claude-sonnet-5-5, at medium effort. No key matches interactive decide (C1). A loop scripts its flags once, and a key can be added later without breaking anything.

verdict.why: Adopted as recommended. Transcription needs less judgment than authoring, so the default follows the catalog on cost: claude-sonnet-5-5 / medium, the tier compliance review uses. No phax.json key, as interactive decide has none (C1); an output or config surface is added only for a named reader (S5), and a key can be added later without breaking anything.
verdict.advocate: The strongest case for own-key: a project on Codex or Vibe would set its writer model once in phax.json instead of passing --model on every call.

arbitratedQuestions.question: Does verdicts mode decide hand-authored artifacts (no sidecar)?

options.label: Yes: the writer returns a hand decision answer and phax writes the blocks in place, as interactive decide does
options.abandons: a single answer form for the new mode: its checks and writer prompt cover the hand decision answer too

options.label: No: refuse a hand-authored artifact with exit 12, naming interactive decide
options.abandons: applying verdicts without a terminal to a hand-authored spec or plan: those callers stay blocked

arbitratedQuestions.rationale: Interactive decide already reads both forms, and approve's open-question lock covers both (C1). The mode should be total on the artifacts decide accepts (S5). The hand-answer checks and the in-place writer exist, so the mode reuses them.

verdict.why: Adopted as recommended. Interactive decide already reads both forms, and approve's open-question lock covers both (C1). The mode stays total on the artifacts decide accepts (S5), reusing the existing hand-answer checks and in-place writer.
verdict.advocate: The strongest case for sidecar-only: the new mode stays smaller, with one answer form to prompt for and check.

settled: Decided by the author on 2026-10-19: the mode lives in phax as a mode of `phax artifact decide`; the person decides and the writer only transcribes (it is not the doctrine's headless mode); a departing verdict still revises the body, so a writer session is needed; phax runs no checker session; deciding never approves, so the artifact stays Draft.

Refusals happen before any session and write nothing. They cover: a verdicts file that is malformed or refused by its `$schema`, one naming another artifact, an unknown or duplicate question, an unlisted option, every refusal interactive decide makes, and the phase guard (exit 1). No terminal is required.

The writer composes the existing decide machinery: doctrine resolution (bundled or project skill, plus `--doctrine`), kept-session resume, the handback document form at the current shape, today's revision and hand-answer checks, one corrective resume, the plan cache re-seed, the path-scoped commit and the decision record. It adds the checks of r-checks, and phax sets `why`, `by` and `at`.
The writer prompt carries the given verdicts and no framing questions. A plan verdict's `phase` is written by the writer and checked against the plan's phases, as today.

Exit families follow interactive decide: 0 committed, 1 phase guard, 5 refused answer after the corrective resume, 8 limits, 12 refusals. The only files left written on failure are those of a failed commit, as today.

The requirements are written for the §9 recommendations. Where the author decides otherwise, the plan follows the decision: r-note follows q-note, r-unnamed q-unnamed, r-why q-why, r-by-* q-by, r-session and r-model q-provider and q-model, r-hand q-hand.

q-off-menu (decided 2026-10-19, implicit): `other` is a reserved id, implicit on every question, never listed and never recommended. A verdict choosing it carries the required note that describes the choice; its why is that note, and its `abandoned` holds every listed option. The output check is that `chosen` is the given option, `other` included. No session ever writes a new option, no document changes shape, and nothing is migrated.
open: The eight §9 questions: q-note, q-unnamed, q-off-menu, q-why, q-by, q-provider, q-model, q-hand.

Left to the plan, as §6 marks indicative: the format id and `$schema` URL of the verdicts file, the `phax artifact schema` argument, the report layout and `--json` key spelling, the commit subject and trailer spelling, and the decision record layout.
constraints: No back-compat shims in persisted schemas. The verdicts format is born with `$schema` and every key required. New record variants are required fields of their variant, never optional fields.

Use explicit per-variant enums. The decision record's `mode` is interactive | verdicts, and each mode carries its own outcome set (interactive: committed | declined | undecided | failed; verdicts: committed | failed).

Each changed format (the verdicts format is new, and decision-record-manifest) is recorded as a `next` snapshot and released by the cut. A verdict's `by` stays { kind: operator, name } (q-by), and hand-decision-answer does not change. spec-document and plan-document keep their shape: only their question checks change, accepting `other` as a chosen id and reserving the id. Whether that check change moves their stamp follows `docs/release.md`; either way nothing is migrated, since every existing document stays valid. Tests must hold across a release cut, so they name current-shape URLs through the release table, never a hard-coded release.

The question checks shared by both document formats, the hand-authored §9 parser and both decide modes accept `other` as `chosen` and refuse an option or recommendation named `other`. The authoring prompt and the phax-spec, phax-planning and decide doctrine skills state the reserved id.

Respect the layers. Reading the verdicts file and stdin goes through ports, and decoding happens at the boundary through an Effect Schema. Matching verdicts to questions and every transcription check are pure domain functions. The CLI command parses, calls one use case and renders.
Interactive decide's behavior, prompt, model rule and attribution are unchanged, apart from accepting a verdict choosing `other`.
Verdicts mode never writes approval records or the `approved` stamp.
`artifact decide` stays classified `refused` by the phase guard in both modes.
Every example and test fixture is made up.

docsPage.reader: A person who already knows their verdicts, or the agent or loop applying them for that person, who wants them recorded without an interactive session and needs to know what to read before approving.
docsPage.example:
cat > verdicts.json <<'EOF'
{ "$schema": "https://docs.phax.run/schemas/decide-verdicts/0.26.0.json",
  "artifact": "docs/specs/2610201015-log-rotation.md",
  "verdicts": [ { "question": "q-keep", "chosen": "keep-20", "note": "Twenty runs cover one release cycle." },
                { "question": "q-scope", "chosen": "per-run", "note": null } ] }
EOF
phax artifact decide docs/specs/2610201015-log-rotation.md --verdicts verdicts.json --by operator
# read the verdicts and the body diff it prints, then:
phax artifact approve docs/specs/2610201015-log-rotation.md --by operator
